newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-AMUNIKE KEEPS BARCELONA IN TOUCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AMUNIKE KEEPS BARCELONA IN TOUCH.

text.p: Substitute Emmanuel Amunike kept Barcelona in the Spanish title race at Logrones on Sunday with an 82nd minute winner.

The 1-0 result left Barcelona six points adrift of leaders Real Madrid, who play at Real Sociedad on Monday. Bobby Robson's side clung on to second place on goal difference ahead of Betis, who had thrashed Rayo Vallecano 4-0 earlier.
Amunike, who has struggled since signing form Sporting Lisbon, headed home his first goal for his new club from a free-kick by midfielder Ivan de la Pena.
But with strikers Ronaldo and Juan Pizzi having a quiet day, Barcelona had been forced to watch struggling Logrones dominate the game with veteran forward Ruben Sosa at the helm.
In the end Logrones ran out of steam, and Amunike's goal was helped by some sloppy work in the home side's defence.

Betis kept up their strong challenge thanks to a second successive league hat-trick by Alfonso Perez, who was given a standing ovation by Rayo Vallecano fans after being substituted towards the end of their side's 4-0 defeat.
Former Ajax winger Finidi George was carried off twice because of heavy challenges and was rated doubtful for the next Betis game.
Deportivo Coruna stayed three points behind in fourth place after Saturday's 1-0 win at Espanyol.
In another game played on Saturday, Atletico Madrid threw away their faint hopes of retaining the league title by crashing 4-1 at home to Valencia.
Atletico are fifth, seven points behind Deportivo and 16 adrift of neighbours Real.
